newsitem.title: USA: State Dept aide quits, admits affair: Post.
newsitem.headline: State Dept aide quits, admits affair: Post.

text.p: The State Department's fifth-ranking official resigned last week after acknowledging a "consensual" relationship with a member of his immediate staff, the Washington Post reported in Monday's editions.

Richard Moose, undersecretary for management, acted after the State Department inspector general looked into allegations in an anonymous letter that Moose had increased his overseas travel accompanied by a female aide with whom he was alleged to be having an affair, the paper said.

The department announced Friday that Moose, a 40-year career foreign service officer who is married and a native of Little Rock, Ark., had resigned to head a study at the Council on Foreign Relations on the impact of declining U.S. foreign policy spending.
Moose, 64, was in charge of all budgetary, administrative and personnel matters at the State Department.
Neither he nor a department spokesman could be reached for comment.
